description: Agent team model agreed 2026-10-24: A7 updated with roles and the hold rule; A8 added for agent buttons. Applied by the Maintenance workflow (apply-issue-updates).

A7.title: Agent handoff: who works on what
A7.what:
Run the project like a small company. Blake (CEO) has the final say: approves merges, decides product questions, and is the only one who clears a hold. Claude (COO) writes briefs into issues, assigns them with labels, reviews builder pull requests and posts a verdict (merge, send back, or Blake's call), and takes the big or sensitive items (security, Rust native code, CI, testing). Codex and Gemini (builders) take one issue and one pull request at a time, only from issues labeled `ready` plus their agent label, following the brief in the issue.

Status lives in labels and pull requests that every agent can read and change (the Roadmap board's Status field needs GraphQL, which agents cannot use): `ready`, `agent:claude` / `agent:codex` / `agent:gemini`, `paused` (with a comment saying why; `needs decision` works the same way). In progress = a draft pull request with "Closes #N"; in review = that pull request marked ready.

**Hold rule:** a failed check, a disputed review or an open question puts `hold` on that pull request, and while any open pull request has `hold`, no agent (Claude included) starts new work. Work in progress stays parked. Only Blake removes `hold`. Blake's direct instruction always overrides the labels: an agent told to take another agent's issue takes it and moves the label to itself.
done: The labels exist with short descriptions
AGENTS.md describes the roles, the one-pull-request-at-a-time rule, the hold rule and Blake's override
The issue health report lists open holds and stale claims (a draft pull request with no activity for a few days)
Tested: an agent refuses to start while a hold exists, and takes another agent's issue when Blake says so

A8.title: Agent buttons: run Claude from anywhere, the team at the Mac
A8.what: An Agents page in the Actions tab so work can be started from GitHub, including from a phone. **Run Claude** runs on GitHub's machines with anthropics/claude-code-action and Blake's subscription token, so it works when the Mac is closed (reviews, tests, labeling, starting builders). **Run Codex** and **Run Gemini** run on Blake's Mac as a GitHub self-hosted runner, using the command-line tools already signed in to his plans (no API keys), so they only work when the Mac is awake. Every button obeys A7's hold rule. Buttons only: no comment-triggered runs, because anyone can comment on a public repo.
